svg.title: Mutual TLS (mTLS)
svg.desc: Mutual TLS (mTLS). Client and server both present certificates, so every connection is authenticated both ways. Step 1, One-way TLS: One-way TLS: the server proves who it is and the channel is encrypted, but the client is anonymous. Step 2, Both sides authenticate: Mutual TLS: the server also asks for a certificate, checks it and reads who the caller is. Step 3, Rejected at the handshake: No certificate, an expired one or an unknown CA: the handshake fails before any request is read. Step 4, Short-lived, auto-rotated: Certificates last an hour and are reissued automatically, so a stolen key soon stops working.

g.text: One-way TLS: the server proves who it is and the channel is encrypted, but the client is anonymous.
Mutual TLS: the server also asks for a certificate, checks it and reads who the caller is.
No certificate, an expired one or an unknown CA: the handshake fails before any request is read.
Certificates last an hour and are reissued automatically, so a stolen key soon stops working.
